answer: A solar irradiance protocol curbs Sybil attacks among sensing agents deployed across juniper and saffron crops. Verifiers evaluate local photovoltaic output against the solar zenith angle to prove each node occupies a discrete physical location. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of maintaining separate solar hardware across dispersed acreage per identity. However, transient cloud cover distorts irradiance readings, causing false rejections of legitimate agents.
